overview:
This wiki explains how a deterministic multitape Turing machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ worst-case time, for a fixed $\kappa = 2^{-182} > 0$. The result matters because the Schönhage–Strassen conjecture, discussed on [its page](nlogn-conjecture.md), holds that $n\log n$ is the optimal growth for multiplication in this model. The bound beats that conjecture, so it is a counterexample to it.

The route has five parts. The first reduces integer multiplication to a carried cyclic convolution of radix-$2^b$ digits, using [the Fourier transform](fourier-transform.md), [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) and [convolution reduction](convolution-reduction.md), with the $O(n\log n)$ [multiplier](harvey-hoeven-multiplier.md) as a subroutine. The second builds the tape procedures that move data, namely [linear network exchange](linear-network-exchange.md), [address interchange](address-interchange.md) and [simultaneous butterfly layers](simultaneous-butterfly-layer.md), whose cost is a power of their parameter below one; [recursive power saving](recursive-power-saving.md) turns that into the exponent. The third places the digits on distinct prime cyclic axes with the [Chinese-remainder address map](chinese-remainder-address-map.md) and rewrites prime-length transforms through [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md) and [Bluestein's chirp identity](bluestein-chirp.md). The fourth lifts the last cyclic coordinate into the [polynomial ring modulo $y^r+1$](polynomial-ring-y.md), where wrap-around is a signed shift, and computes transforms there with the [synthetic polynomial transform](synthetic-transform.md) and [signed Kronecker packing](kronecker-packing.md). The fifth recovers the exact product by [rounding](rounding-recovery.md) the approximate coefficients, whose error is below $1/2$, and then propagating carries.

parts.title: Background: transforms and convolution
parts.intro: The reader needs the conjecture that the target beats, the $O(n\log n)$ multiplier used as a black box, and the transform vocabulary. [The discrete Fourier transform](fourier-transform.md) and [the butterfly operation](butterfly-operation.md) give the basic fast-transform step, and [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) is the operation the whole argument reduces to. [Multiplication as convolution of digits](convolution-reduction.md) shows that the integer product is a carried convolution, which is the first main step.

parts.title: Tape address procedures
parts.intro: These procedures move data on a multitape machine at cost $O(V)$ times a power of their parameter, and they are the only source of the saving in running time. [Linear network exchange](linear-network-exchange.md) and [lower-triangular factorization](lower-triangular-factorization.md) supply the linear-algebra core, and [address shear](address-shear.md) turns it into an exchange of address fields. [Address interchange](address-interchange.md) and [simultaneous butterfly layers](simultaneous-butterfly-layer.md) use these to swap fields and apply butterflies to all records at once, and [recursive power saving](recursive-power-saving.md) combines them into the recursion that gives an exponent below one.

parts.title: Prime axes and prime-length transforms
parts.intro: The digit sequence must be placed where a cyclic convolution can be computed with transforms of convenient length. The [Chinese-remainder address map](chinese-remainder-address-map.md) places it on distinct prime cyclic axes using address interchanges. [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md) then rewrites a prime-length transform as a multidimensional transform with power-of-two axes, and [Bluestein's chirp identity](bluestein-chirp.md) turns the middle transform into a normalized cyclic convolution.

parts.title: Polynomial ring and synthetic transforms
parts.intro: The last cyclic coordinate is lifted into a polynomial ring in which multiplying by a power of $y$ is a signed shift, so wrap-around costs no multiplication. The [polynomial ring modulo $y^r+1$](polynomial-ring-y.md) provides this ring, and the [synthetic transform](synthetic-transform.md) over it uses only signed shifts and butterfly additions. [Signed Kronecker packing](kronecker-packing.md) then turns products over the ring into integer products that the $O(n\log n)$ multiplier can compute.

parts.title: Exact recovery and the main result
parts.intro: This part closes the argument. [Rounding recovery](rounding-recovery.md) shows that the coefficient error is below $1/2$, so rounding and carries give the exact binary product. [The target page](integer-multiplication-target.md) then assembles the earlier pages into the $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ bound and states the result in full.
